findings.title: Dynamic code execution via eval()
findings.description: eval() executes arbitrary Python from a string. If any part of the string originates from user input, an attacker achieves remote code execution.

findings.title: Raw SQL string built from request input
findings.description: A SQL statement is assembled with Python string formatting and then executed. Any interpolated value lets an attacker alter the query.
findings.snippet:
term = request.args.get('q', '')
    sql = f"SELECT * FROM reports WHERE title LIKE '%{term}%'"
    rows = session.execute(text(sql)).all()

findings.title: Subprocess called with shell=True
findings.description: shell=True passes the command to a shell, so any interpolated argument is interpreted as shell syntax.

findings.title: View missing @csrf_exempt protection audit
findings.description: This view mutates state over POST but does not declare a CSRF policy, so it relies entirely on framework defaults.

findings.title: Vulnerable dependency: jinja2 2.11.0 (CVE-2024-22195)
findings.description: jinja2 before 3.1.3 allows attribute access to bypass the sandbox via str.format. A sandboxed template rendering untrusted input is exploitable.

findings.title: Vulnerable dependency: django 3.2.18 (CVE-2023-46695)
findings.description: Django before 4.2.5 allows a denial of service via a crafted multipart form. Publicly disclosed with a working proof of concept.

findings.title: Telnet service enabled
findings.description: The device configuration enables telnet, which transmits credentials in clear text.

findings.title: DEBUG mode enabled in production settings
findings.description: DEBUG = True returns full stack traces to the client, leaking file paths, settings, and query text.
